errors: "Neither PR linked its issue, so neither issue closed when the PR merged" asserts an unverified closure history.
"A crash that can't happen on any build you ship" extends the evidence about current builds to older builds.
"Nothing tracks the bug any more" overlooks the retained closed issue.
R01.note: Explains each release blocker, but repeats the gate explanation and overstates what closing erases.

errors: "Nobody treats it as actionable work anymore" is not established by removal from open filters.
"Leaving them open costs nothing else" is unsupported and contradicts the other consequences it lists.
"The crash was never fixed" is not established by raising the minimum Android version.
"This one isn't stale at all" confuses inactivity with whether the bug still occurs.
R02.note: Names the release cost, but leaves issue identities unexplained and substitutes unsupported absolutes for evidence.

R03.note: Clearly compares the consequences for each issue and distinguishes unsupported old builds from a fixed crash.

R04.note: Gives a concise, accurate explanation of the release gate and the different closure decisions.

errors: "Neither PR referenced its issue, so both stayed open" asserts an unverified causal closure history.
"No session picks it up" is an unsupported prediction.
"Closing as 'stale' would imply it went away on its own" assigns an unsupported meaning to that closure.
"The real consequence is you are dropping Android 9" incorrectly attributes an existing v3.0 support change to closing the issue.
R05.note: Explains the cost of leaving completed work open, but adds speculative consequences and repeats the correction.

errors: "Each one should only be closed" when its work is finished contradicts the permitted won't-fix outcome.
"That PR never referenced the issue, so it didn't close it" assumes the precise closure history.
"Android 9 users ... can't hit this crash" overlooks users running older builds.
"Closing it as stale would only make the release gate pass" ignores the other open milestone issues.
R06.note: Provides an actionable fix plan, but inaccurately describes closure as necessarily recording finished work.

errors: "While #401-#404 are in it, release stays blocked" omits that they must remain open.
"There's nothing to fix on supported versions" goes beyond evidence that Android 9 cannot install current builds.
R07.note: Connects open issues to the release gate, but unnecessarily makes authorized fixes and completed closures await confirmation.

errors: "Closing it would only hide it" overstates the effect on a retained, readable issue.
"The release gate would pass with a known bug in it" ignores the other open milestone issues.
R08.note: Offers a clear next action for each issue, though the live bug's closure consequences are overstated.

errors: "That PR never referenced #402, so GitHub never closed it" asserts an unverified closure history.
"A real bug disappears from the tracker" incorrectly describes a closed issue as disappearing.
"No fix is planned" is not among the verified facts.
"V3.0 removed on purpose" asserts intent beyond the verified minimum-version change.
R09.note: Makes the release costs explicit, but invents planning information and parks a reproducible bug awaiting a decision.

errors: "Neither PR referenced its issue, so the issues never got closed" asserts an unverified closure history.
"The crash can't occur on an installable build anymore" overlooks older builds.
"No current user can hit" overlooks users still running older builds.
"The flash ships to every dark-mode user on cold start" generalizes one reproduction to every user.
"The tracker loses the only record of it" invents record exclusivity and ignores the retained closed issue.
"Nobody has filed it in 8 months, so no second report is coming" invents reporting history and predicts future reports without evidence.
R10.note: Answers the requested comparison, but severely undermines it with invented evidence and predictions.
